notes.title: Road Map: Three New Game Modes Coming to Space Tourist!
notes.content:
[p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121460/148172d2fe1de288dd842a51341a0fb2c1a1e035.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Since launch, [i]Space Tourist[/i] has been about wonder — flying across the stars, landing on mysterious worlds, planting flags, and capturing the beauty of the unknown. [/p][p]I'm excited to officially announce that three new game modes are coming to [i]Space Tourist[/i] — each offering a fresh way to play, with unique objectives and flavour, all while staying true to the game’s relaxed, immersive spirit.[/p][hr][/hr][h2]The Roadmap[/h2][p][/p][h3][b]The Tourist[/b] (Available Now)[/h3][p]This is the original [i]Space Tourist[/i] experience. No pressure, no goals — just pure exploration. Fly. Land. Wander. Photograph. Reflect.
[/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]Coming Next: The Cartographer[/b][/h3][quote][p][i]“You’ve been everywhere. Now it’s time to leave your mark.”[/i][/p][/quote][p]In this new mode, you’ll become a planetary surveyor.
Your mission? Complete [i]exploration contracts[/i] — this mode gives purpose to your wanderings — and turns your journal into a badge of honour.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Release window[/b]: Later this year. [/p][hr][/hr][h3][b]In Development: The Investigator[/b][/h3][quote][p][i]“Something’s out there. Follow the trail.”[/i][/p][/quote][p]A strange echo has been detected — a low, pulsing signal that seems to ripple across the galaxy.
No one knows what’s generating it, or why it’s moving. But one thing’s certain: it’s leaving a trail.[/p][p]In this narrative-driven mode, you’ll follow a breadcrumb trail of distant coordinates, tracking the echo across carefully selected systems. Each stop offers a clue — a moment — a piece of the puzzle.[/p][p]Your journey might uncover:[/p][list][*][p]Abandoned research posts[/p][/*][*][p]Mysterious planetary events[/p][/*][*][p]Lost messages and encoded data[/p][/*][*][p]Or something far older than you expected…[/p][/*][/list][p]This is a slower, more meditative mode — perfect for explorers who want mystery over mechanics, and wonder over weapons.[/p][p]More details coming soon.[/p][hr][/hr][h3] [b]In Development: The Survivor[/b][/h3][quote][p][i]“Low fuel. No backup. Get home or die trying.”[/i][/p][/quote][p]The galaxy isn’t always gentle. In [i]The Survivor[/i], you’ll start with a damaged spacesuit and limited fuel.
To survive, you’ll need to land on dangerous planets, scavenge rare fuel deposits, and manage each jump carefully as you limp toward your home system.
This is a resource-light, risk-heavy challenge mode — where exploration isn’t optional, it’s survival.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]Final Thoughts[/h3][p]These new game modes are designed to expand [i]Space Tourist[/i] in gentle, modular ways — layering meaning and structure onto the systems you already know, without compromising the calm, meditative tone.[/p][p]They’re not replacing the core game — they’re giving you new roles to play [i]within[/i] this beautiful universe.[/p][p]I'd love your feedback as we shape what’s next.[/p][p]Much love,
Rhys [/p][p][i]Grow Now![/i][/p]

notes.title: Patch Notes 20.05.25
notes.content:
[h1]Key Fixes & Improvements:[/h1]

[h3]Smoother UI Interactions:[/h3]

[list]
[*] The Pause Menu (ESC) now correctly takes precedence. If your Journal or Solar System Map view is open, opening the Pause Menu will now seamlessly close these other views first.
[*] Similarly, the Journal ('J') will no longer open if the Pause Menu or the Solar System Map View ('TAB') is already active, preventing UI clashes.
[*] The Solar System Map View ('TAB') will now automatically close an open Journal before activating, ensuring a clear view.
[*] Fixed an issue where the Pause Menu could shrink to a tiny size when opened. This was related to game pausing (Time.timeScale) affecting UI animators; relevant animators have been updated to use unscaled time.
[*] The mouse cursor will now correctly hide when the Solar System Map View ('TAB') is active. It will also consistently become visible when UI panels like the "Update Info" screen are closed, ensuring you can always interact with underlying menus.
[/list]

[h3]Player Control Consistency:[/h3]

[list]
[*] Resolved a bizarre bug where player movement could remain locked every other time after opening and closing the Solar System Map View. Player movement lock state is now managed more consistently across all UI interactions (Journal, Map View, Pause Menu).
[*] When teleporting to a bookmarked system via the Journal, the player will now have its movement speed set to zero upon arrival for safer and more predictable fast travel.
[/list]

[h3]Journal Enhancements:[/h3]
[list]
[*] The Journal ('J') will now correctly display only bookmarked solar systems that belong to your current galaxy seed. No more seeing old bookmarks from previous voyages in your current log!
[*] Fixed issues with the Journal's scrollable list where buttons might overlap or not display correctly. The layout should now be much more reliable.
[/list]

[h3]Bookmark Feature Refinements:[/h3]

[list]
[*] The key to bookmark a system is now 'B' (previously 'U').
[*] When a system is bookmarked (or if it's already bookmarked), a confirmation message ("[System Name] BOOKMARKED" or "[System Name] ALREADY BOOKMARKED") will now briefly appear on screen for 5 seconds.
[/list]


 As always, thank you for your feedback and happy exploring!

notes.title: Captain’s Log Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121460/c5eae538c08b65d3714be024b99edeac462c34f4.png[/img]

I'm thrilled to announce the launch of the Captain's Log Update – a set of new tools designed to help you master the vastness of space and keep track of your favourite locations. 

[h2][b]What's New?[/b][/h2]

[b]Bookmark Your Universe (Press 'B' in a System):[/b]
Stumbled upon a breathtaking solar system? A place that feels like home? Press 'B' while you're within a solar system to add its coordinates and name to your Captain's Log. 

[b]Your Personal Captain's Journal (Press 'J'):[/b]
The galaxy is vast, but your memory doesn't have to be! The new in-game Journal allows you to keep a running list of your most important system discoveries.

[b]Instantaneous Return Jumps:[/b]
Open your Journal ('J'), select a previously bookmarked system from your scrollable list, and with a single click, you'll be instantly transported to the outskirts of that system, perfectly positioned and facing the star. Your movement will be set to zero upon arrival, giving you full control.

[b]In-Game Update Notes:[/b]
I've added a handy "What's New?" panel accessible from the main interface so you can always catch up on the latest features.

[b]Fixes & Polish:[/b]
Fixed an issue where player movement could get stuck in a locked state after repeatedly opening and closing UI panels. Player controls should now be much more consistent.
Improved UI panel interactions for a smoother experience.

Chart it, mark it, and navigate it with ease.

Thanks for playing!

Grow Now!

notes.title: Steam Cloud Saves Are Live!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121460/74d25cb980cc2557c85b9e4a0249b14bb0547067.png[/img]


Just a small but useful update today:

Space Tourist now supports Steam Cloud Saves.
Your progress — planets visited, systems explored, photos taken, flags planted — will now sync across devices automatically.

So whether you're switching between machines, reinstalling, or just want a bit of peace of mind, your save data will come with you.

That’s it! Thanks for playing and exploring the galaxy 💫

More to come!

– Rhys

notes.title: Achievements Are Here!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121460/dfb5137d1a73880c63ecc032b0a85a69294e7ebd.png[/img]


I’ve just pushed an update that adds a whole bunch of Steam Achievements to Space Tourist!

You’ll now be rewarded for all sorts of galactic milestones — whether you're hopping systems, landing on mysterious comets, snapping gorgeous planetary shots, or boldly planting flags where no one else has.

🏆 Here’s just a few things you can now unlock:

"First Contact" – land on your very first planet

"Galactic Photographer" – take 100 in-game photos

"Universal Claim" – plant flags on 800 different worlds (yes, really)

"Comet Rider" – if you find one, you’ll know 😉


If you’ve already made loads of progress, don’t worry: the game remembers where you've been — and achievements will unlock automatically the next time you load in or land somewhere new.

As always, thank you so much for playing. Space Tourist is still growing and you’re part of the adventure.

See you in the stars 🚀
– Rhys (aka the dev)

notes.title: The Comet Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121460/9b6a5e614fbae4b8a9323973219a4a6e15a604b0.png[/img]

This has to be my favourite update so far - just looking up from a planet and seeing an icy comet fly blisteringly overhead is awe-inspiring! 

I've obviously played this game for many hours now and I found my self taking a tonne of photos!


[list]
[*] Comets are now flying around the galaxy, you may be fortunate to spot one when you are in a system!
[*] Yes you can land on them, but they can be incredibly fast-  faster than your jetpack! TIP:  You may want to stand in the comet's path and allow it to fly into you!
[*] Use the comets like super fast taxis - getting you from one end of a solar system to the other in record time! 
[/list]

Enjoy!

Other fixes:
I've also optimised planetary trees so they load much faster and are more performant.

notes.title: No more floating trees + choose your camera reel size
notes.content:
So after yesterday's minor patch fix with adding a music volume slider and fullscreen/window support, here is the first small update/patch:

[h3]Main changes:[/h3]
[list]
[*] No more floating trees or rocks! As strange as that was, all planetary objects are now firmly rooted!
[*]  Choose your photo reel size before you start your next expedition. The camera reel size decides the length of your expedition run. Once all photos have been taken, the expedition ends. Less photos means a quicker run. 
[*]  Solar System Map Upgrades. You can now zoom in and rotate the solar system map to get a closer look at the planets of the system you are currently in. 
[*]  The music transitions have now added fade down at the end of each track to avoid abrupt changes. 
[/list]

That's it! More to come! 

Soon I'll be implementing some sort of save system and moons and flying comets!

notes.title: Development Update: Atmospheric Planets, Oceans & Campfires
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121460/8bc5cd2209a5258b6b1c4aa7a6b223a4cec6fd16.png[/img]

I'm excited to share some big news about Space Tourist. I've been hard at work adding in new features to the game. Today I'm unveiling three new features that will make your exploration of the Serene Nebula even more immersive.

🌠 [b]Revamped Planet Generation [/b]
I've completely reworked the planet generation system to make each world more intriguing and diverse. You'll encounter a variety of landscapes—from rugged mountains to serene valleys.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121460/1d9d7efc6385d4289f45993d82d7379a281b3a1f.png[/img]

🌌 [b]Atmospheric Planets[/b]
There is a chance now that some systems will have atmospheric planets. Watch the local star set on the horizon, see clouds drift across alien skies. There is also a chance that the planets will have some flora. 

🌊 [b]Swimmable Oceans[/b]
Many planets now feature oceans that you can explore. Swim through alien seas, discover underwater landscapes. 

🔥 [b]Campfires Under the Stars[/b]
After a day of discovery, there's nothing like relaxing by a campfire on an alien world. Set up camp, enjoy the warmth of the fire, and gaze up at unfamiliar stars in the night sky.

These additions aim to make your journey through Space Tourist even more memorable. My goal is to create a peaceful and cosy experience for everyone who sets out to explore the stars in Space Tourist.

Thank you for your support. Stay tuned for more updates as we get closer to launch in Spring next year. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45121460/e7ee6132ad1e7f31ae4a990a630e7a36409bb42b.png[/img]
